page: Amazon Web Services c3.8xlarge is a legacy compute-optimized instance hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz, supplying 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The system configuration includes 60.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent with zero GPUs present. For temporary high-speed scratch space, the instance provides 640 GB of bundled local SSD storage, alongside a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that single-core performance on this older x86_64 architecture is limited, with Geekbench single-core testing scoring 705.0 and stress-ng single-core ranking in the lower quartile. Single-threaded data handling reflects this trait, yielding 21.55 GB/s in gzip compression. However, parallel workloads utilize all 32 vCPUs effectively, achieving mid-tier results across PassMark CPU (24090.95), Geekbench multi-core (6961.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (109.19 GB/s). The system also delivered 10.23 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 19.96 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Given the compute-focused ratio of roughly 1.88 GB of memory per core and integrated local SSD capacity, the c3.8xlarge fits legacy multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation, and parallel web serving that do not require modern vector instruction sets like AVX-512. Lower single-thread IPC and architectural age reduce its qualitative compute efficiency relative to modern alternatives, but its high thread count and bundled storage remain functional for distributed utility tasks.

While architectural age limits its single-thread efficiency relative to newer generations, its high thread density and bundled local storage make it suitable for multi-threaded batch compute, parallel compilation, caching tiers, and distributed web serving.
